summary: Tokenized generate and embedding batch wrappers arrived at stamp_http_worker_ipc with rids=None. The existing code stamped only each child request, leaving wrapper rids and http_worker_ipcs unset. The fix derives missing wrapper rids from the child requests and stamps wrapper-level routes while preserving explicit rids. The actual current split-output path remains a BaseBatchReq and already routes through http_worker_ipcs, so no unsupported scalar http_worker_ipc field was added.

tests.what_was_measured: Failing-before reproduction against the checked-out stamp_http_worker_ipc implementation: generate and embedding tokenized batches retained rids=None and http_worker_ipcs=None; the empty-batch boundary also failed. Raw output: reports/j-5f8fb395a7d9/evidence/failing-before.log

9 tests and 2 subtests passed after the fix, covering generate and embedding tokenized batches, preservation of explicit wrapper rids, and an empty tokenized batch. Raw output: reports/j-5f8fb395a7d9/evidence/passing-after.log
The changed implementation and regression test compile successfully.
All repository formatting, lint, safety, and registered-test validation hooks applicable to the changed files passed.

A source-checkout server on one gfx950 GPU with --tokenizer-worker-num 2 and --enable-tokenizer-batch-encode became ready. A native two-item input_ids /generate batch returned HTTP 200 with two results and six completion tokens each. The server log records a two-sequence GPU prefill. Raw request/response, launch metadata, fixture manifest, and server log are retained under reports/j-5f8fb395a7d9/evidence/.

remaining_limitations: The GPU serving validation used the campaign-qualified deterministic two-layer random Llama fixture. It validates HTTP transport, multi-tokenizer routing, batch tokenization, and engine execution only; it does not validate semantic accuracy or another model architecture.
Only one assigned gfx950 GPU was used. No tensor-parallel, data-parallel, multi-GPU, or multi-node workload was claimed or tested.
No native C++ or FlyDSL source changed, so a native rebuild was not relevant.

The upstream proposed PR https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/27995 remains open. Its current approach is related; this change was independently reproduced and validated against the prepared mirror base.
